predecessors.name: House of Habsburg
predecessors.text: the Burgundian Netherlands (Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg) held by Philip the Handsome under Maximilian I as regent, which Cliopatria draws under this row from 1487

successors.name: Austrian Empire
successors.text: the Habsburg lands as they stood until the Peace of Pressburg of 26 December 1805; Cliopatria's Austrian Empire row starts in 1806

ledger.x: 1487: the Habsburg monarchy appears, at its first Cliopatria shape, the Netherlands of Philip the Handsome 'with his father Maximilian I as regent (1482-1493)'.
1492: 22 cells of the eastern Netherlands leave the Habsburg shape.
23 May 1493: the Treaty of Senlis returns the County of Burgundy, Artois, Charolais and Noyers to the Habsburgs.
1507: no Cliopatria shape in this row until 1516; the house-of-habsburg row draws the Netherlands and the Austrian lands together for 1507-1515.
1516: the Austrian hereditary lands are drawn as the Habsburg monarchy (the house-of-habsburg row ends 1515).
1519: Franche-Comte is drawn with the Austrian lands.
1526: Ferdinand is elected king of Bohemia (infobox 'Acquisition of Bohemia and Hungary: 1526'; text 'In 1526, Ferdinand was elected king of Bohemia and Hungary').
1527: Ferdinand invades Hungary, 'which led to the capture of Buda and several other key settlements along the Danube'.
1529: Overijssel and Guelders come into the Netherlands shape.
1536: Groningen.
1547: Royal Hungary is drawn as Habsburg land, because Cliopatria's Kingdom of Hungary row ends in 1546 and its 1556 shape here already holds it.
27 July 1552: Temesvar falls to the Ottomans after a siege.
1556: Charles V's abdication leaves the Netherlands to Philip II.
1572: 47 cells of north-east Hungary join the Habsburg shape in the year after Cliopatria's Eastern Hungarian Kingdom row ends (1571).
1583: the court moves from Vienna to Prague.
1596: Eger falls to the Ottomans.
1597: the Long Turkish War takes ground.
1597: Pápa, Tata, Győr and Veszprém taken from the Ottomans (the page: 'in 1597').
1600: the border fortress of Kanizsa falls to the Ottomans.
1606: the Long Turkish War ends at Zsitvatorok: 'the war did not yield significant territorial changes'.
1612: the court returns from Prague to Vienna (the page: Prague was the capital 1583-1611).
31 July 1619: the Bohemian Confederacy forms and the revolt becomes a contest between two states.

31 July 1619: Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia leave Habsburg rule as the Bohemian Confederacy forms ('on 31 July 1619 at Prague, these states formed the Bohemian Confederacy', Frederick V page).
September 1620: Saxon troops occupy Lusatia for the emperor.
November 1620: White Mountain.
November 1620: the rebel Bohemian army is destroyed at White Mountain.

31 December 1621: the Peace of Nikolsburg gives Gabriel Bethlen of Transylvania 'seven counties around the Upper Tisza River', 'the fortresses of Tokaj, Munkacs, and Ecsed' and 'a duchy in Silesia' (page, signed 31 December 1621; the Principality of Transylvania page: 'seven additional counties in northern Hungary').
By the end of 1627: Wallenstein 'had occupied Mecklenburg, Pomerania, and Jutland'; in early 1628 'Ferdinand deposed the hereditary Duke of Mecklenburg and appointed Wallenstein in his place'.
By the end of 1627: Wallenstein 'had occupied ...
June 1629: 'The Treaty of Lubeck let Christian IV keep Schleswig and Holstein' on 'relatively lenient terms'; the page does not say when Jutland was cleared, which the lenient terms imply.
1631: the imperial hold on Mecklenburg ends in Cliopatria's shape (gone by 1632); the page has 'Gustavus landed in Pomerania in June 1630' but does not say when Mecklenburg was lost.
1632: Silesia leaves the shape until 1636.
1635: the Peace of Prague.
1636: Saxony's occupation of Lusatia ends in cession.
1636: Ferdinand cedes Lusatia to Saxony in perpetuity ('Under the Traditionsrezess annex of 1636, Ferdinand ceded both territories in perpetuity', Peace of Prague page; treaty dated 30 May 1635).
1639: 'In April 1639, Banér defeated the Saxons at Chemnitz, then invaded Bohemia in May.'
1642: the north Bohemian cells return in Cliopatria's shape.
24 October 1648: Westphalia.
1663-64: the war 'saw Nové Zámky fall and Moravia invaded, ending at St.
1673: 30 cells of Trento and Bolzano join the Habsburg shape.
19 November 1682: Thokoly's Principality of Upper Hungary is established and Upper Hungary leaves Habsburg control.
14 July 1683: 'The main Ottoman army finally laid siege to Vienna on 14 July 1683.'
19 August 1685: 'Nové Zámky (Érsekújvár): The fortress fell.'
15 October 1685: Thokoly's principality ends and Upper Hungary returns to the Habsburgs.

2 September 1686: 'After resisting for 78 days, the city [Buda] fell on 2 September', and Turkish resistance 'collapsed as far as Transylvania and Serbia'; 'Charles V, Duke of Lorraine, won the Second Battle of Mohács' in 1687 (no day).
1688: 'The Holy League captured Belgrade from the Ottomans in 1688.'
1690: 'The Ottomans retook it in 1690, during the distraction of the war with Louis XIV.'
August 1691: Slankamen.
January 1699: Karlowitz.
26 January 1699: 'Signed: 26 January 1699' at Karlowitz.
1700: 'The Croatian and Bihać borders were agreed by mid-1700', the Temesvar borders 'by early 1701'; the Ottomans 'largely confined to the south of the Sava River'.
February 1702: the Austrian army in Lombardy forces the French behind the Adda.
By late September 1703 Rakoczi's rising holds land: 'By late September 1703, his forces controlled most of the Kingdom of Hungary east and north of the Danube.'
1704: Austria occupies Bavaria after Blenheim.
March 1707: Austria takes the Duchy of Milan.
April 1707: imperial troops take the Kingdom of Naples.
1708: Mantua passes to the Habsburgs.

1 May 1711: the end of Rakoczi's War of Independence (infobox); Rakoczi had left the Kingdom of Hungary for Poland on 21 February 1711 and the page names the Treaty of Szatmar as the settlement without a date.
1713: the Southern Netherlands become Austrian ('the Austrian Netherlands in 1714').
Rastatt: 'The Spanish territories in Italy: Naples, Milan, and Sardinia.
11 April 1713: parts of the Duchy of Milan pass to Savoy.
11 April 1713: Utrecht gives Austria the French border towns of Flanders.
7 March 1714: Rastatt restores the Bavarian elector.
5 August 1716: the Austro-Turkish War takes ground at Petrovaradin.
October 1716: Prince Eugene conquers the Banat.
August 1717: Spain lands on Sardinia.
21 July 1718: Passarowitz.
21 July 1718: 'Territory passed from Wallachia to the Habsburg Monarchy: Oltenia (Lesser Wallachia).'
21 July 1718: the Treaty of Passarowitz ends the war.
17 February 1720: Sicily passes to the Habsburgs in exchange for Sardinia.
17 February 1720: the Treaty of The Hague ends the Spanish occupation of Sardinia.
17 February 1720: Austria cedes Sardinia to Savoy in exchange for Sicily.
October 1733: French and Savoyard troops enter the Duchy of Milan.
1734: Naples and Sicily are lost to the Spanish Bourbons in the War of the Polish Succession.
May 1735: the Presidi are lost to the Bourbons.
1737: the Austro-Turkish War of '1737-1739' begins (the page: the treaty 'ended the Austro-Turkish War (1737-1739)').
18 November 1738: Parma passes to Austria.
November 1738: the Treaty of Vienna ends the Franco-Sardinian occupation of Milanese land ('ratified in the Treaty of Vienna in November 1738').
November 1738: the Treaty of Vienna gives Sardinia Novara and Tortona.
18 September 1739: Belgrade.
18 September 1739: Oltenia is given up (the Passarowitz page: 'Oltenia was returned to Wallachia').
18 September 1739: the treaty 'ended the Austro-Turkish War (1737-1739)'.
16 December 1740: Prussia 'invaded Silesia without a formal declaration of war'.
14 September 1741: 'the Franco-Bavarian force captured Linz'.
26 November 1741: 'the French under Maurice de Saxe took Prague', which let Charles Albert be crowned King of Bohemia.
1742: Habsburg forces expel Duke Francesco III of Modena and hold the duchy.
12 February 1742: Austrian troops take Munich on the day Charles Albert is crowned emperor.
June 1742: 'the Treaty of Breslau ended the First Silesian War'.
June 1742: the First Silesian War ends at Breslau.
December 1742: Austria recaptured Prague (the text places this in December, the year implied 1742).
13 September 1743: Worms.
15 August 1744: Prussia invades Bohemia in the Second Silesian War.
October 1744: Charles VII regains Munich.
Late 1744: the Prussians abandon Prague and give up Bohemia.
18 October 1748: 'on 18 October 1748, the war ended with the signing of the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle', which gave the 'Duchy of Parma and Piacenza' to Infante Philip.
18 October 1748: the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle restores the Duke of Modena.
18 April 1757: Prussia marches into Bohemia.
Summer 1757: after Kolin the Prussians leave Bohemia.
August 1772: the First Partition.

January 1775: Austria 'obtained roughly 10,000 km2 of Moldavian territory, which it called Bukowina' and 'formally annexed' it that month (10,442 km2); the 2 July 1776 Palamutka convention returned 59 villages and kept 278.
1778: William Bolts founds an Austrian colony on the Nicobar Islands.
January 1778: Austria claims Lower Bavaria under a secret agreement with Charles Theodore.
13 May 1779: the Treaty of Teschen ends the War of the Bavarian Succession ('signed on 13 May 1779'); Maria Theresa 'returned Lower Bavaria to Charles Theodore, but kept the so-called Innviertel'.
13 May 1779: Austria keeps the Innviertel ('a 2,200-square-kilometer (850 mi2) strip of land in the drainage basin of the Inn river').
1783: the Austrian colony on the Nicobar Islands ends.
1788: the Austro-Turkish War ('the 1788-91 war').
1791: Sistova.
1791: Sistova gives the Austrians Orșova and two small Croatian border towns.

18 September 1794: the Austrian Netherlands were 'annexed after the Battle of Sprimont in 1794, that was followed by the Peace of Basel in 1795'; 'De facto Habsburg rule ended with the annexation by the revolutionary French First Republic in 1795'; 'Austria relinquished all of its claims on the province in 1797…
24 October 1795: 'their representatives signed a treaty, dividing the remaining territories of the Commonwealth': 'the Austrian 47,000 km2 with 1.2 million and Lublin and Kraków' (6.41%).
1796: Lombardy leaves the shape.
17 October 1797: Campo Formio.
27 April 1799: Austrian and Russian forces occupy the Cisalpine Republic.
20 June 1799: Austro-Russian troops conquer Piedmont.
30 May 1800: the Austrians leave the Cisalpine Republic.
20 June 1800: the Piedmontese Republic is re-established ('The Piedmontese Republic was re-established on 20 June 1800'; 'In 1800, Napoleon returned to Italy, taking back much of the new republics').
1803: the Electorate of Salzburg 'had been under Habsburg rule since 1803'.
25 February 1803: the Breisgau passes from Austria to the Duke of Modena.
1804: the Habsburg monarchy becomes the Austrian Empire.
26 December 1805: Pressburg.
26 December 1805: 'Venetia, Istria, and Dalmatia were incorporated into the Kingdom of Italy.'
26 December 1805: 'Scattered Austrian holdings in Swabia went to Württemberg and Baden' ('passed to French allies').
26 December 1805: the Swabian holdings are shared between Württemberg and Baden (the page does not split them).
26 December 1805: the Electorate of Salzburg is annexed.
26 December 1805: 'The Austrian Empire annexed the Electorate of Salzburg', whose elector, the Emperor's brother, received the Duchy of Würzburg.
1805: the Habsburg Monarchy row ends; the same state continues as the Austrian Empire (Cliopatria row from 1806, 'dissolved' only in 1918 on the page).

wars.name: Ottoman-Habsburg wars, Hungary phase
wars.outcome: After Mohacs (1526) Ferdinand is elected king of Bohemia and Hungary; he takes Buda in 1527; the Ottomans abandon the siege of Vienna on 14 October 1529 with no territory changed; after Buda falls in 1541 the central and southern counties go to the Sultan and…

wars.name: Long Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Austrians take Pápa, Tata, Győr and Veszprém in 1597; by 1605 only Raab remains in their hands; Zsitvatorok (1606) yields no significant territorial change.

wars.name: Bohemian Revolt
wars.outcome: The Estates depose Ferdinand (August 1619), crown Frederick, and lose at White Mountain in November 1620; Saxony, promised Lusatia in July 1620 ('in return for the cession of Lusatia'), occupies it in September 1620 and holds it as a pledge until the 1636…

wars.name: Thirty Years' War (Habsburg lands)
wars.outcome: Peace of Lubeck (June 1629) lets Christian IV keep Schleswig and Holstein; Peace of Prague (1635); Westphalia, 24 October 1648: peace with France and Sweden, France annexes the Decapole and Sundgau.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1663-1664)
wars.outcome: The war 'saw Nové Zámky fall and Moravia invaded, ending at St.

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Ottomans besiege Vienna from 14 July 1683; the Holy League takes Nové Zámky (19 August 1685), Buda (2 September 1686), wins at Mohacs (1687), Slankamen (August 1691) and Zenta (11 September 1697); Karlowitz gives the Austrians 'the rest of Hungary and…

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession (Austrian share)
wars.outcome: Rastatt (7 March 1714): Austria receives 'Naples, Milan, and Sardinia' and the Spanish Netherlands, and Freiburg from France; France keeps Landau.

wars.name: Rakoczi's War of Independence
wars.outcome: The rising begins on 15 June 1703; by late September 1703 its forces hold most of the Kingdom of Hungary east and north of the Danube, then conquer Transdanubia; the Diet at Szecseny (September 1705) elects Rakoczi ruling prince of the Confederated Estates…

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1716-1718)
wars.outcome: Passarowitz (21 July 1718): the Habsburgs gain the Banat of Temeswar, western Wallachia (Oltenia), northern Serbia with Belgrade and northern Bosnia (Posavina).

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1737-1739)
wars.outcome: Belgrade (18 September 1739): the Habsburgs give up the Banat of Craiova (Oltenia), the Kingdom of Serbia with Belgrade and the Bosnian Posavina; the border becomes the Sava and Danube.

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession
wars.outcome: Prussia invades Silesia on 16 December 1740; Franco-Bavarian forces take Linz (14 September 1741) and Prague (26 November 1741); Breslau (June 1742) ends the first Silesian war; Austria recovers Prague in December 1742; Worms (13 September 1743) cedes lands…

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1788-1791)
wars.outcome: Sistova (1791): the Austrians, who had occupied Bosnia, Belgrade and Bucharest, keep only Orșova and two small towns on the Croatian frontier.

wars.name: War of the First Coalition (Austrian share)
wars.outcome: Campo Formio (17 October 1797): Austria cedes the Austrian Netherlands, recognises the Cisalpine and Ligurian Republics, and receives Venice, the Terraferma, Istria, Dalmatia and the Bay of Kotor.

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition (Austrian share)
wars.outcome: Pressburg (26 December 1805): Venetia, Istria and Dalmatia to the Kingdom of Italy, Tyrol and Vorarlberg to Bavaria, Swabian holdings to Wurttemberg and Baden; Austria annexes Salzburg; a 40 million franc indemnity.

certainty.note: The Ottoman frontier in Hungary (Royal Hungary after 1541), the imperial exclaves in Swabia and the Netherlands' frontier with France moved by campaign, not survey; the 1648 line with France is the exception only at Westphalia.

After Karlowitz 'commissions' set the Croatian and Bihac borders (mid-1700) and the Temesvar borders (early 1701); the Belgrade treaty set the Sava and Danube line (1739); partition lines in Poland (1772, 1795) and Bukovina (1775-76…
